Class 5 · Chapter 7 of 10

Elapsed time, timetables and dates

Separate actual time, displayed time and calendar intervals.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Convert and compare measurements. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can find elapsed time.
  • I can correct clock errors and switch time formats.
  • I can use a calendar and timetable.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Elapsed time

A drone leaves at 6:30 a.m. and arrives at 10:50 a.m.

6:30 to 10:30 is 4 hours. 10:30 to 10:50 is 20 minutes.

The trip takes 4 hours 20 minutes.

Screen 2 of 4

The 24-hour clock

After 12:00 noon the 24-hour clock keeps counting: 13:00, 14:00 and so on.

To change 14:15 to 12-hour time, take away 12.

14:15 is 2:15 p.m.

Screen 3 of 4

Slow clocks

A slow clock shows too little time, so add the gap.

This clock shows 3:00 and is 45 minutes slow.

The true time is 3:45.

Screen 4 of 4

Dates and days

A week has 7 days. Add 7 to a date and you get the same weekday.

In March 2026 the 1st is a Sunday.

So the 12th is a Thursday.

Words to know
elapsed time
How much time has passed from the start to the end.
24-hour clock
A way of telling time that counts from 00:00 to 23:59.
slow clock
A clock that shows an earlier time than the true time.

For parents

What your child learns

Total time adds each stage. 35 + 18 + 12 = 65 minutes, which is 1 h 5 min. Calendars repeat each week, so dates a week apart fall on the same weekday.

A common slip

Children often write 65 minutes as 1 h 65 min. Subtract 60 and carry 1 hour. On a calendar, add 7 to find the next same weekday.

5-minute home activity: Calendar count

  1. Draw a month calendar on paper.
  2. Highlight every Saturday.
  3. Count how many Saturdays it has.
  4. Add three task times and write the total in hours and minutes.
